evidence.quote: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

summary.short: Minnesota session law (2025 1st Special Session, ch. 12) regulating data centers: permitting coordination, water-appropriation conditions for large data centers, utility tariffs and energy-standard treatment, an annual fee on qualified large-scale data centers, and sales tax exemption changes. Most sections take effect the day following final enactment.
summary.long: Chapter 12 (HF 16) of the Laws of Minnesota 2025, 1st Special Session, regulates data centers. Sections 1, 2, 5 and 6 state that data-center permitting inquiries are referred to the Minnesota Business First Stop Program and direct agency permitting staff to be made aware of this policy. Sections 3-4 set water-appropriation rules for data centers with consumptive use above 100,000,000 gallons per year, covering preapplication information requests, evaluation of water availability, permit conditions on public health and water conservation, and possible aquifer tests. Section 7 defines a data center as a facility designed to have a load of 100 megawatts or more. Sections 9-10 require the commission to define a very large customer class by December 15, 2026, allow it to approve or reject tariffs for such customers, and require utilities to offer a clean energy and capacity tariff. Sections 11-15 exclude qualified large-scale data centers from solar-standard calculations and energy-conservation contributions, and direct fee revenue to the energy and conservation account. Section 16 imposes an annual fee on qualified large-scale data centers by peak demand, in four tiers from $2,000,000 to $5,000,000. Section 17 extends sales and use tax exemptions to qualified large-scale data centers (at least $250,000,000 invested within 60 months after June 30, 2025), conditioned on prevailing wages and green-building certification within three years of service, with repayment if certification is not met. Most sections take effect the day following final enactment; the sales tax changes apply to purchases made after June 30, 2025.

notes: Session law (2025 1st Special Session, ch. 12, H.F. 16) that adds and amends provisions in several chapters. Source text marks changes with new text begin/deleted text begin markers; the new insertions are the operative change. Points to note: (1) 'data center' in 216B.02 subd. 11 (facility designed for a load of 100 megawatts or more) and 'qualified large-scale data center' in 297A.68 subd. 42(f) (25,000 square feet and 250,000,000 dollars within 60 months) are separate definitions; 216B.02 subd. 12 refers to 297A.68 subd. 42(f). (2) 297A.68 subd. 42(g) allows the exemption for purchases within 35 years of the first qualifying purchase, while (h) allows the exemption only for facilities certified before July 1, 2042. (3) Several 'commissioner' and 'the department' references (e.g., Secs. 1, 3, 4, 16) are not tied to a named agency in this text. Effective dates: most sections take effect the day following final enactment; Secs. 17 and 18 apply to sales and purchases made after June 30, 2025. Presented to the governor June 12, 2025; signed June 14, 2025.
